lines: KEYPOINTS
Enzymes arebiological ororganiccatalysts.Theyaremadeofproteinsand
can speed up the rate of chemical reactions without themselves being
chemicallychangedattheendofthereactions.
Enzymes are specific in their actions because of the shape of their active
sites.Only substances with shapes complementary to that of active site
can fit intotheenzymemolecules and beactedupon bytheenzymes.
Factors affecting the rate of enzyme catalyzed reactions are temperature,
pH,enzymeconcentration and substrateconcentration.
Every enzyme has its optimum temperature and pH. At optimum
temperatureandpH,an enzyme works atthegreatestspeed.
When temperature rises well above the optimum temperature, the
protein structure of enzyme is denatured and so the rate of reaction
decreasesrapidly.
Enzymes are specific in action.They are specific not only for substrate but
alsoforthekindofreaction.
Intracellular enzymes e.g,mitochondrial enzymes work inside the cells
whileextracellular enzymes e.g.pepsin arereleased from thecelland they
workoutsidethecell.
Cofactors are the non-protein molecules required by enzymes for their
action.
The cofactors called prosthetic groups make permanent attachment with
the enzyme while the cofactors called coenzymes are not permanently
attachedtotheenzyme.
An enzyme attaches with the substrate to form enzyme-substrate (ES)
complex.The active site of enzyme catalyzes the reaction and substrate is
convertedtoproduct.
The lock and key model of enzyme action states that the substrate
molecule exactly fits in the active site of enzyme which is a rigid and non-
flexiblestructure.
Theinducedfit model suggeststhat the enzymemolecule alters the shape
of active site slightly so that it fits more tightly around the substrate
malecule.
